messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] KMS API error spike detected in us-east-1. Increase in 5xx/504s for GenerateDataKey and Encrypt calls — error rate 42% (5m). Paging oncall: @emma :rotating_light:
emma: ack. i'm on it. paging @raj for SRE assist. what's the customer impact so far?
raj: digging in. seeing tons of failed startups with `unable to sign request: KMS unreachable` from the bootstrap decrypt path. Also elevated 502s at the edge when signing client requests. sample log: ```2026-03-15T12:00:03Z ERROR bootstrap decrypt failed: rpc error: code=Unavailable msg="KMS: 504 Gateway" service=infra-startup instance=i-0abcd````
maria: existing long-lived instances seem fine (they keep cached keys). New instances that call KMS at boot are failing to finish startup -> autoscaler retries -> more KMS traffic. likely a burst + throttling loop.
oliver: confirms. looking at CloudWatch/Stackdriver metrics: KMS p99 latency spikes and a rise in ThrottledRequests. This matches a provider-side throttling event.
brianna: do we have any temporary knobs? we can short-circuit the bootstrap to use cached keys for 10m while provider recovers. there's an internal feature flag `use_local_key_cache` for the startup path.
emma: good idea. prepare for a controlled flip. i'll coordinate canary then full. raj, can you add client-side backoff adjustments as a quick patch?
raj: yes. plan: 1) flip `use_local_key_cache` for service `inference-startup` -> canary 10% 12:06 UTC 2) increase SDK retry ceiling + add decorrelated jitter (maxRetries=8, base=200ms) 3) enable token bucket rate limiter for KMS calls to prevent retry storm.
ops-bot: Runbook command to flip flag (requires infra-api token): ```curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.internal/api/flags" -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRA_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"flag":"use_local_key_cache","env":"prod","service":"inference-startup","value":true}'```
emma: i'm initiating canary now. rolling to 10% in us-east-1. monitoring dashboards.
incident-bot: Canary deploy started: 10% users in inference-startup. KMS error rate (us-east-1) -> 35% (1m)
maria: after canary, observed reduced failed startups in the canary group. overall KMS error rate trending down to 22%. some customer-facing 502s still showing (initial request only).
raj: patch rolled to increase retries + token bucket limiter applied to node bootstrap. cfg snippet applied: ```kms:
  max_retries: 8
  backoff_base_ms: 200
  token_bucket:
    rate: 50 # req/s
    burst: 100
```
oliver: also added a short local cache TTL bump for decrypted bootstrap secrets to 15m to avoid repeated KMS hits for immediate restarts.
brianna: monitoring shows error rate now 12% and startup failure rate reduced by ~90% in the last 10m.
emma: good. i'm going to page infra-eng to open a support ticket with provider and get an ETA. @raj please keep retry and limiter config until provider confirms.
raj: will keep on. adding enhanced logging for KMS call latencies for postmortem.
incident-bot: Provider status check: AWS KMS reported elevated latency in us-east-1 earlier, now showing degraded performance (status page link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/).
maria: Customer impact summary for post-incident note: "New node startups in Dedicated pools experienced bootstrap failures due to KMS API latency/throttling, causing delayed capacity and transient 502s for some customers on first requests. Mitigation (local key cache + client-side rate limiting + retries) reduced impact; no data was exposed."
emma: oncall handoff: i need to step out at 12:30 UTC. handing to @oliver. Oliver, you own monitoring + provider follow-up.
oliver: taking over. i'll keep flags enabled and coordinate with provider support. opening ticket reference: RDW-INC-20260315-KMS-01.
brianna: quick note for SRE followups: 1) add client-side reservoir sampling to flatten startup bursts 2) bake local key cache into startup path permanently as opt-in 3) run chaos tests for KMS throttling scenarios
emaria: also recommend we add SLA-safe fallback behavior in the signing library to queue requests briefly instead of failing fast — avoids 502 propagation to customers.
emaria: (typo above — maria)
emaria: tagging for postmortem: @raj @brianna @oliver @emma @maria (ops)
emma: thanks team. i have left the incident channel to oliver. next steps: runbook updates, provider ticket updates, and postmortem in 48h. closing pager for me. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: action created: RDW-ACTION-4521 "Implement client-side KMS rate limiting & persistent startup cache" assigned to @brianna, due in 7 days.
incident-bot: KMS error rate in us-east-1 now 6% (last 5m). No new startup failures in the last 5m. Monitoring will remain on for 2 hours.
oliver: holding until provider confirms resolution. will post status updates in this thread.
